scenarios.description: Two-replica actor get-or-create/invoke/owner-control/spawn full chain over real HTTP: isolated TS and Rust Router sides each consume the same canonical actor-routing projection, drive the identical actor-full-chain-acceptance service through real HTTP into two real Runtime replicas (test-only relays), and must produce identical HTTP step results, projected semantic frame sequences (ephemeral correlation ids tokenized per key, timestamps normalized, payloads hashed, handshake/health frames excluded), seeded Mongo state/audit and terminal behavior.

knownDifferences.description: After a failed actor create, the retained entry's second request fails at a different Router stage: TS resolves the retained entry at getOrCreate and defers activation to the method invoke (failure surfaces via actor.owner.failure); Rust re-activates at the next getOrCreate (ACK rejected -> actor.getOrCreate.error). Both implementations fail closed and the HTTP-observable status/body are identical (flaky http.steps equal PASS).
knownDifferences.evidence: actor_parity_full_chain flaky steps: TS getOrCreate.error code ActorCreateFailed + actor.owner.failure path; Rust getOrCreate.error code AckRejected path. HTTP responses both UnhandledServiceError platform errors.
owners: TS: router/src/router/actorGetCreateActivationCoordinator.ts + actorMethodDispatcher.ts (deferred activation on retained entries)
knownDifferences.resolution: accepted by root 2026-08-03: recorded difference, both fail closed with identical HTTP observables; Rust is the only implementation after cutover, no separate semantic fix; revisit only if future TS alignment is required.

knownDifferences.description: Rejected activateInitial ACK produces a different actor.getOrCreate.error code: TS ActorCreateFailed vs Rust AckRejected. Wire-level vocabulary difference in a fail-closed path; HTTP-observable platform error is identical.
knownDifferences.evidence: TS error frame code ActorCreateFailed (message carries runtime reason); Rust error frame code AckRejected (message actor get-or-create failed closed).
owners: Rust: ActorActivationRequestBroker waiter outcome vocabulary (AckRejected, pinned by activation corpus)
knownDifferences.resolution: accepted by root 2026-08-03: recorded difference; Rust activation corpus vocabulary remains frozen; revisit only if future TS alignment is required.

nonBlockingFollowUps.description: On the success path both sides produce the same frame set; independent sub-flows (spawn submit/return, owner.invoke/control) arrive in non-semantic async order, so raw relay-order comparison yields ordering false positives. Future improvement: canonical per-HTTP-step window ordering in the actor parity projection (not implemented in this batch to avoid masking semantic differences).
